answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy makes identity costly to multiply: every new identity must lock scarce, unrecoverable stake before it can be trusted, and that stake is slashed the moment one of its claims is judged false. A hollow swarm of cheap clones therefore burns the kernel of shared trust, and the harbor of escrow only admits identities already at risk. An attacker pays once per fake persona, forever, so faking identity stops being profitable.
